headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are unlikely.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js is a document-processing viewer with PDF-file I/O and browser-based tests, while RisingWave has no documented shared channel, filesystem bridge, or message path to ingest pdf.js outputs. With no shared communication surface, prompt injection between the pair is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects pdf.js output into RisingWave as trusted instructions, reassess upward.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe rendered PDF text into any instruction parser.
Add provenance labels if a bridge is introduced.
requires-engineering: enforce channel separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and can read PDF files, but RisingWave lists no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is not evidenced; uncertainty remains because RisingWave’s runtime data handling is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same host directory, leakage risk increases.
IF RisingWave is later configured to ingest pdf.js-produced files, reassess upward.
mitigations: Store each agent’s files in separate directories.
Avoid placing sensitive PDFs in a shared workspace.
Review any future mount or sync configuration.
requires-engineering: add access controls between workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances but only documents PDF-file access and no network egress; RisingWave documents no write surfaces or concurrency model. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources such as shared filesystem writes, git state, or OAuth scopes, so direct capability conflict appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF either agent gains shared database or git write privileges, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disjoint.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Serialize any future writes through one owner.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js is a document-processing component, so its outputs may be consumed downstream, but RisingWave is not documented as treating those outputs as authoritative or taking actions from them. Without a verified pipeline from pdf.js into RisingWave, cascading error is possible only through an added integration, not by default.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests pdf.js output without validation, cascading errors become more likely.
IF pdf.js-derived text is used as source data for automated transformations, reassess upward.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any handoff.
Require schema checks on extracted PDF text.
Keep human review for high-impact outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance and verification metadata.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented in either profile: pdf.js lists PDF document handling with no secrets or residency claims, and RisingWave lists no data classes, retention, or jurisdictional constraints. Because the profiles do not establish a regulated-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent, reassess compliance obligations.
IF residency, retention, or certification constraints are added to RisingWave, re-evaluate the pair.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Avoid routing regulated data through undocumented paths.
Review residency and retention settings if added.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated data.
